question.text: \(f(x)\) is a differentiable function and given \(f^{\prime}(2)=6\) and \(f^{\prime}(1)=4\), then \(L=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{f\left(2+2 h+h^2\right)-f(2)}{f\left(1+h-h^2\right)-f(1)}\)

solution.text:
Hint: \(\operatorname{It}_{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{f\left(2+2 h+h^2\right)-f(2)}{f\left(1+h-h^2\right)-f(1)} \quad[\div(\) form \()]\)
by L. Hospital rule.
\(\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{It}_{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{f^{\prime}\left(2+2 h+h^2\right)(2 h+2)}{f^{\prime}\left(1+h-h^2\right)(1-2 h)} & =\frac{f^{\prime}(2)}{f^{\prime}(1)} \times\left(\frac{2}{1}\right) \\
& =\frac{6}{4} \times 2=3
\end{aligned}\)
